key_insight: Embedding graph-based turbine interactions into the Kriging mean improves sparse-data prediction and sample efficiency in wind farm layout optimization.
engineering_relevance: The approach can reduce the high-fidelity aerodynamic evaluations needed to design wind farm layouts for greater annual energy production (AEP).
method: Represent the farm as a directed graph of aerodynamic turbine interactions.
Assemble low-dimensional pairwise interactions into a farm-scale surrogate mean.
Use a Gaussian process to model residuals and uncertainty for Bayesian optimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports competitive IEA Wind Task 37 benchmark solutions with about 280 AEP evaluations, gains over ordinary and multi-fidelity Kriging in a controlled 16-turbine case, and an extension to 48 turbines.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well reusable pairwise interactions capture the aerodynamics of the target farm and operating conditions.
paper_title: A Graph-informed Kriging model for sample-efficient Bayesian optimization of wind farm layouts
